portat: portō, -āre — to carry, bear, bring (3rd sg. pres.)
portusque: portus, -ūs (m.) — harbour, port (acc. pl.; also nom. sg./pl.) + -que, and
poscere: poscō, -ere, poposcī — to demand, ask for (pres. inf.)
poscit: poscō, -ere, poposcī — to demand, claim, call for (3rd sg. pres.)
posse: possum, posse, potuī — to be able, can (pres. inf.)
postrema: postrēmus, -a, -um — last, hindmost (f. nom. sg.; also n. nom./acc. pl.)
praecepta: praecipiō, -ere, -cēpī, -ceptum — to advise, warn; praeceptum, -ī (n.), warning, precept (acc. pl.)
primas: prīmus, -a, -um — first, foremost (f. acc. pl., with arces)
primum: prīmus, -a, -um — first; prīmum (adv.), first, at first (n. acc. sg. as adv.)
prisca: priscus, -a, -um — ancient, of the old days, old-fashioned (f. nom. sg., with fidēs)
processit: prōcēdō, -ere, -cessī, -cessum — to go forward, advance; of time, pass (3rd sg. perf.)
promittere: prōmittō, -ere, -mīsī, -missum — to promise, offer, hold out (pres. inf.)
pubes: pūbēs, -is (f.) — young men, youth, the grown men (nom. sg.)
pudor: pudor, pudōris (m.) — shame, modesty, sense of honour (nom. sg.; also voc. sg., personified Pudor)
pugnae: pugna, -ae (f.) — fight, battle, combat (gen. sg.; also dat. sg., nom. pl.)
qua: quā (adv.) — where, by which way; in any way (after sī); also quī/quis, f. abl. sg. · also indef. after sī, any (f. nom. sg.; n. nom./acc. pl.: sī qua nūmina) · also after nē, in any way (nē qua) · also indef. adj. after nē, any (f. nom. sg.: nē qua mora; n. nom. pl.: nē qua … dispendia) · also interrog. adj. in indirect question, by what? (f. abl. sg.: qua ratione) · also rel. (f. abl. sg.: malum qua non aliud)
quae: quī, quae, quod — who, which (rel., f. nom. sg.; f./n. nom./acc. pl.) · interrog. adj., what? which? (f. nom. sg.: quae sententia) · also interrog. adj., n. nom. pl. (quae sint ea nūmina) · also exclam. adj., n. acc. pl. (quae bella exhausta canebat!; quae … regna) · also interrog. pron./adj., n. acc. pl., what? (quae quibus anteferam; quae … maiora) · also f. nom. pl. (quae … acies)
quaecumque: quīcumque, quaecumque, quodcumque — whoever, whatever (f. nom. sg.; n. nom./acc. pl.)
quaerit: quaerō, -ere, quaesīvī, quaesītum — to seek, look for, ask (3rd sg. pres.)
qualis: quālis, -e — of what sort; such as, like, as (m./f. nom. sg.)
quem: quī, quae, quod — who, whom (rel. or interrog., m. acc. sg.) · quis, quid after sī, nē — any(one), some(one) (indef., m. acc. sg.: sī quem)
qui: quī, quae, quod — who, which (rel. pron., m. nom. sg./pl.) · interrog. adj./pron., who? which? (m. nom. sg./pl.: Sed vos qui tandem) · also exclam. adj., what (youths)! (m. nom. pl.: Quī iuvenēs!)
quid: quis, quid — who, what (interrog., n. nom./acc. sg.) · also adverbially, why? (n. acc. sg.) · also indef. after sī, anything (n. nom./acc. sg.: sī quid) · also indef. after nē, anything (nē quid inexpertum)
quis: quī, quae, quod — who (rel., dat./abl. pl., old form = quibus); also quis, who? (interrog.) · also indefinite quis, anyone (after nē/neu, m. nom. sg.); quis locus, which place? (interrog. adj.) · also indef. after sī, anyone (m. nom. sg.: sī quis) · also indef. after quam (m. nom. sg.: quam quis, until anyone) · also indef. after rel. quae (m. nom. sg.: quae quis, whatever any man)
quisquis: quisquis, quidquid — whoever, whatever (m./f. nom. sg.)
quo: quī, quae, quod — who, which, what (rel. or interrog., m./n. abl. sg.); quō (adv.), where to · also indef. after nē, any (abl. sg.: nē quō nūmine) · also quō, to what end? why? (quō molem … statuēre?) · also quō (conj.), in order that (quō … averteret)
quod: quī, quae, quod — which (rel., n. nom./acc. sg.); quod (conj.), because, that · also interrog. adj., what? (n. nom./acc. sg.: quod genus) · also acc. of respect, wherefore (quod tē per superōs … ōrō) · also indef. adj. after sī, any (n. nom. sg.: sī quod nūmen) · also connective, but, now (quod sī, 'but if'; n. acc. sg. as conj.)
rabies: rabiēs, -ēī (f.) — rage, frenzy, raving hunger (nom. sg.)
ratione: ratiō, -ōnis (f.) — reckoning, plan, method, way (abl. sg.)
relicta: relinquō, -ere, relīquī, relictum — to leave behind, abandon (perf. pass. part., f. abl. sg.)
rumpe: rumpō, -ere, rūpī, ruptum — to break, burst, break off (sg. imper.)
rutulo: Rutulus, -a, -um — Rutulian, of the Rutuli, Turnus's people (m. abl. sg., with sanguine)
sacra: sacrum, -ī (n.) — holy thing, rite; pl. sacra, sacred rites (nom. pl.) · also acc. pl. (sacra … commendat) · also sacer, sacra, sacrum — holy, sacred; accursed (f. nom. sg.: sacra tellus; auri sacra famēs) · also sacer, sacra, sacrum — holy (n. acc. pl.: sacra ostia)
sacrata: sacrō, -āre — to consecrate, hallow (perf. pass. part., f. abl. sg.) · also n. acc. pl. (sacrāta … iūra)
saeva: saevus, -a, -um — fierce, savage, cruel (n. acc. pl.) · also f. abl. sg. (Gorgone saevā); n. nom./acc. pl. · also f. nom. sg. (dea saeva)
saevit: saeviō, -īre, -iī, -ītum — to rage, be fierce, storm (3rd sg. pres.)
sanguine: sanguis, sanguinis (m.) — blood; descent, lineage (abl. sg.)
satis: satis (indecl. n., adv.) — enough, sufficient; adv., sufficiently
saturnia: Sāturnius, -a, -um — of Saturn; Sāturnia, daughter of Saturn, Juno (f. nom. sg.)
sceptra: scēptrum, -ī (n.) — sceptre; royal power (acc./nom. pl., often for sg.)
se: suī (reflexive pron.) — himself, herself, itself, themselves (acc.; also abl. sē)
secant: secō, secāre, secuī, sectum — to cut, cut up (3rd pl. pres.)
secuit: secō, -āre, secuī, sectum — to cut, cleave, cut through (3rd sg. perf.)
secutus: sequor, sequī, secūtus sum — to follow, pursue (perf. part., m. nom. sg., deponent)
sed: sed (conj.) — but; sed enim, but indeed
sedebat: sedeō, -ēre, sēdī, sessum — to sit, sit still (3rd sg. impf.)
sedemque: sēdēs, -is (f.) — seat, abode, dwelling place, site (acc. sg.) + -que, and
sequor: sequor, sequī, secūtus sum — to follow, pursue, go after (1st sg. pres. of deponent)
sequuntur: sequor, sequī, secūtus sum — to follow (3rd pl. pres., deponent)
sese: sē, sēsē — emphatic reflexive, himself, itself, themselves (acc.)
sic: sīc (adv.) — so, thus, in this way
sidera: sīdus, sīderis (n.) — star, constellation; pl. the sky (acc./nom. pl.)
sine: sine (prep. + abl.) — without · also sinō, -ere, sīvī, situm, to allow, let (sg. imper.: sine palmula)
siqua: sī + qua — if any, if in any way (indef. qua, f. nom. sg., with gloria)
solve: solvō, -ere, solvī, solūtum — to loosen, release, free from (sg. imper.)
spumantem: spūmō, -āre — to foam, froth (pres. part., f. acc. sg.)
struere: struō, -ere, struxī, structum — to pile up, arrange, make ready (pres. inf.)
stygii: Stygius, -a, -um — of the Styx, Stygian, infernal (m. nom. pl.)
sub: sub (prep.) — + abl. under, beneath; + acc. up to, under
summa: summus, -a, -um — highest, topmost; surface of (f. abl. sg.; n. nom./acc. pl.) · also f. nom. sg. (rēs summa; summa diēs)
summoque: summus, -a, -um — highest, topmost, uppermost (m./n. abl. sg.) + -que, and
super: super (adv. and prep.) — above, over; besides, in addition · also remaining, left over (sōla mei super imāgō) · also prep. + abl., about, concerning (quam super adventū; multa super nātā)
supra: suprā (adv., prep. + acc.) — above, over, on top
surgens: surgō, -ere, surrexī, surrectum — to rise, spring up (pres. part., m. nom. sg.)
sustulit: tollō, -ere, sustulī, sublātum — to raise, lift up (3rd sg. perf.)
tacitum: tacitus, -a, -um — silent, unspoken, secret (n. nom./acc. sg.; m. acc. sg.)
tali: tālis, -e — such, of such a kind (m./f./n. abl. sg.; n. dat. sg.)
tam: tam (adv.) — so, so much, to such a degree
tanta: tantus, -a, -um — so great, such (f. nom. sg.; n. nom./acc. pl.) · also f. abl. sg. (ex tantā urbe)
tantos: tantus, -a, -um — so great, so much (m. acc. pl.)
tardum: tardus, -a, -um — slow, sluggish, lingering (m. acc. sg.; n. nom./acc. sg.)
tegit: tegō, -ere, tēxī, tēctum — to cover, shield (3rd sg. pres.)
tela: tēlum, -ī (n.) — missile, weapon, spear, dart (acc./nom. pl.)
tempestas: tempestās, tempestātis (f.) — storm, weather, season (nom. sg.)
tempus: tempus, -oris (n.) — time, season, hour (nom. sg.) · also n. acc. sg. (tempus inane peto)
tenens: teneō, tenēre, tenuī — to hold (pres. part., nom. sg.)
teucri: Teucer, Teucrī (m.) — Teucer, early king of Troy (gen. sg.) · also Teucrī, -ōrum (m. pl.) Trojans (voc. pl.: Teucrī, secludite) · also m. nom. pl. (Teucrī, Trojans)
teucrum: Teucrī, -ōrum (m. pl.) — Teucrians, Trojans (gen. pl., archaic -um for -ōrum)
thracius: Thrācius, -a, -um — Thracian, of Thrace (m. nom. sg.)
torquet: torqueō, torquēre, torsī, tortum — to twist, whirl, hurl (3rd sg. pres.)
totum: tōtus, -a, -um — whole, entire (m. acc. sg.; n. nom./acc. sg.)
tua: tuus, -a, -um — your, yours (sg. poss.) (f. nom. sg.) · also n. acc. pl. (tua nūmina) · also f. abl. sg. (tua laude)
tuenti: tueor, tuērī, tuitus sum — to look at, watch; tuens, one looking (pres. part., m. dat. sg., with tibi)
tum: tum (adv.) — then, at that time; next
turbata: turbō, -āre — to disturb, throw into confusion (perf. pass. part., n. nom./acc. pl.; f. nom./abl. sg.)
turbidus: turbidus, -a, -um — stormy, wild, confused, turbulent (m. nom. sg.)
turne: Turnus, -ī (m.) — Turnus, king of the Rutulians, rival of Aeneas for Lavinia (voc. sg.)
turni: Turnus, -ī (m.) — Turnus, king of the Rutuli, Latinus's rival for Lavinia (gen. sg.)
turnum: Turnus, -ī (m.) — Turnus, king of the Rutulians, rival of Aeneas for Lavinia (acc. sg.)
turnus: Turnus, -ī (m.) — Turnus, young king of the Rutulians, suitor of Lavinia (nom. sg.)
tyrrhidae: Tyrrhidēs, -ae (m.) — son of Tyrrhus, a Tyrrhid (patronymic; nom. pl., with pueri)
ullo: ūllus, -a, -um — any (m. abl. sg., with alumnō)
ultro: ultrō (adv.) — of one's own accord, voluntarily; besides
urbes: urbs, urbis (f.) — city (nom. pl.; also acc. pl.)
ut: ut (conj.) — + subj. so that, in order that; + indic. as, when, how
veluti: velut, velutī (adv.) — just as, as when
venti: ventus, -ī (m.) — wind (nom. pl.; gen. sg.) · also voc. pl., in address (sine nūmine, ventī)
vero: vērō (adv.) — in truth, indeed, but; tum vērō, then indeed
vertice: vertex, verticis (m.) — peak, summit; whirl (abl. sg.)
vertitur: vertō, vertere, vertī, versum — to turn; vertitur, wheels round (3rd sg. pres. pass.)
video: videō, -ēre, vīdī, vīsum — to see, behold (1st sg. pres.)
vocibus: vōx, vōcis (f.) — voice; word, utterance (abl./dat. pl.)
volans: volō, -āre — to fly (pres. part., m. nom. sg.) · also f. nom. sg. (columba volāns)
volcanus: Volcānus (Vulcānus), -ī (m.) — Vulcan, god of fire; fire, flame (nom. sg.)
volvitur: volvō, volvere, volvī, volūtum — to roll, tumble (3rd sg. pres. pass.)
